title: LAST-MILE LOGISTICS INDUSTRY DEVELOPMENT ACT
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to improve citizens’ quality of life and to contribute to the development of the national economy, by creating foundations for developing the last-mile logistics industry and by promoting the rights and interests of last-mile delivery service workers and consumers.

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended on Jan. 16, 2024>
  1. "Last-mile logistics services" means activities relating to logistics defined in Article 2(1)1 of the Framework Act on Logistics Policies, which are providing, at the request of consumers, the services of delivering mostly small-size, low-weight goods through the process of collecting, packaging, storing, sorting, etc. and the services of directly delivering them using two-wheeled motor vehicles or brokering such delivery through information and communications networks, etc.;
  2. "Last-mile logistics industry" means the industry that creates economic or social value added through last-mile delivery service activities;
  3. "Last-mile logistics business" means the following business which provides last-mile logistics services at a cost:
  a. Package delivery service business: The business of delivering goods through the process of collecting, sorting, etc. by using trucks for the trucking transport service permitted pursuant to Article 3(1) of the Trucking Transport Business Act;
  b. Small package delivery agency service business: Business of delivering cargo directly by using two-wheeled vehicles under Article 3(1)5 of the Motor Vehicle Management Act, drones under Article 2(1)1 of the Act on the Promotion of Utilization of Drones and Formation of Infrastructure (hereinafter referred to as "drones") or outdoor mobile robots defined in subparagraph 4-2 of Article 2 of the Act on the Promotion of Development and Distribution of Intelligent Robots (hereinafter referred to as "outdoor mobile robot") or of mediating such deliveries by utilizing information and communications networks, etc.;
  4. "Last-mile logistics business operator" means any of the following business providers who conduct the last-mile logistics business:
  a. A package delivery service provider: A person who has filed for registration of the package delivery service business pursuant to Article 5(1) after obtaining permission for the trucking transport services under Article 3(1) of the Trucking Transport Business Act;
  b. A certified small package delivery agent service provider: A person who has obtained certification as a small package delivery agent service provider pursuant to Article 17(1);
  5. "Business office" means an entity that concludes a contract with a package delivery service provider or a certified small package delivery agent service provider and performs outsourced business activities regarding last-mile logistics services, such as collection and delivery of goods, within a certain allocated area;
  6. "Last-mile delivery service worker" means each of the following persons who engage in the last-mile logistics business:
  a. A package delivery service worker: A person who engages in the services of collecting, delivering, etc. of goods under a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services, a contract for employment, etc., or any other similar contract concluded with a package delivery service provider, a business office, etc.;
  b. A small package delivery agent service worker: A person who engages in the services of delivering, etc. of goods under a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services, a contract for employment, or any other similar contract concluded with a certified small package delivery agent service provider or a business office;
  7. "Last-mile logistics facilities" means facilities used in conducting the last-mile logistics business for collecting, loading and unloading, sorting, storing, delivering, etc. of goods, among logistics facilities defined in subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Act on the Development and Management of Logistics Facilities.

Article 3 (Responsibilities of the State and local governments) (1) The State and local governments shall formulate and implement policies necessary for the development and promotion of the last-mile logistics industry.
  (2) The State and local governments shall endeavor to enhance the rights and interests of last-mile delivery service workers and strengthen their safety and to promote the rights and interests of consumers.
  (3) The State and local governments shall endeavor to promote last-mile logistics services in areas prescribed by Presidential Decree (hereinafter referred to as "logistically vulnerable areas"), which are difficult to provide last-mile logistics services due to inconvenience in the transportation system, such as islands and mountain areas. <Added on Oct. 24, 2023>
  (4) Last-mile logistics business operators shall endeavor to create a sound and transparent market for last-mile logistics services, to enhance the rights and interests of last-mile delivery service workers and strengthen their safety, and to promote the rights and interests of consumers and shall actively cooperate in the Government's policies for such purposes. <Amended on Oct. 24, 2023>

Article 4 (Relationship to other statutes) (1) Notwithstanding the provisions of this Act, the Trucking Transport Business Act shall take precedence with regard to the trucking transport business, such as permission for the trucking transport business to provide last-mile logistics services and the management of transport employees.
  (2) Except as provided in this Act, the Act on the Development and Management of Logistics Facilities shall apply to last-mile logistics facilities.

CHAPTER II PACKAGE DELIVERY SERVICE BUSINESS

Article 5 (Registration of package delivery service business) (1) A person who intends to engage in the package delivery service business by using trucks that are used for the trucking transport service provided by a person with permission under Article 3(1) of the Trucking Transport Business Act (hereinafter referred to as "trucks dedicated to package delivery services"), only for the purpose of collecting and delivering goods eligible for package delivery service business, shall satisfy the following requirements and file for registration of his or her business with the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport as prescribed by Presidential Decree: <Amended on Jan. 16, 2024>
  1. The person shall obtain permission for the trucking transport service pursuant to Article 3(1) of the Trucking Transport Business Act;
  2. The person shall meet the standards prescribed by Presidential Decree for facilities, equipment, business offices, etc.;
  3. Where the person intends to use drones or outdoor mobility robots for the collection and delivery of cargo, he or she shall meet the requirements prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as registration of ultra-light aircraft rental services under Article 48 of the Aviation Business Act or operation safety certification under Article 40-2 of the Intelligent Robot Development and Distribution Promotion Act.
  (2) Where a person who has filed for registration pursuant to paragraph (1) intends to change any registered matter, he or she shall file for registration of such change with the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, as prescribed by Presidential Decree; provided, the foregoing shall not apply where such person changes any minor matter prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall issue a registration certificate, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, to a person who has filed for registration of his or her package delivery service business or has filed for registration of change thereof pursuant to paragraph (1) or (2).
  (4) A package delivery service provider shall file a report on matters relating to the requirements for registration under paragraph (1) with the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport within three years from the date of registration under paragraph (1), as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 6 (Grounds for disqualification from filing for registration) None of the following persons shall file for registration of the package delivery service business under Article 5(1):
  1. A person specified in any subparagraph of Article 4 of the Trucking Transport Business Act;
  2. A person for whom two years have not passed since his or her imprisonment with labor or heavier punishment declared by a court for violation of this Act was completely executed (or deemed completely executed) or since the person was exempted from the execution of such sentence;
  3. A person who is under suspension of the execution of his or her imprisonment with labor or heavier punishment, declared by a court for violation of this Act;
  4. A person for whom two years have not passed since the registration was revoked under Article 15(1);
  5. A corporation with an executive officer who falls under any of subparagraphs 1 through 4.

Article 7 (Prohibition of lending of package delivery service business registration certificate) No person shall conduct any of the following acts:
  1. Allowing another person to conduct package delivery service business under his or her name or trade name or lending his or her certificate of registration to another person;
  2. Conducting package delivery service business under another person's name or trade name or borrowing another person's certificate of registration;
  3. Assisting another person in conducting an act described in subparagraph 1 or 2.

Article 8 (Package delivery service provider's outsourcing of services and liability for compensation) (1) A package delivery service provider may outsource business activities that need to be done, to a business office or a package delivery service worker for the efficient performance of his or her package delivery service business.
  (2) A business office to which services are outsourced by a package delivery service provider under paragraph (1) may sub-outsource goods collection services, delivery services, or any other business activities that need to be done, to a package delivery service worker.
  (3) Where a business office or a package delivery service worker in providing services under an outsourcing contract has intentionally or negligently lost or damaged goods in the course of collecting or delivering them, thereby causing damage to a consumer, the package delivery service provider shall be liable to compensate the consumer for the damage jointly with the business office or the package delivery service worker.
  (4) Where the package delivery service provider has paid compensation for the damage pursuant to paragraph (3), such provider may exercise a right of indemnity against the business office or package delivery service provider liable to pay compensation for the damage.

Article 9 (Management of business offices) (1) A package delivery service provider shall supervise a business office to which business activities are outsourced pursuant to Article 8, as to whether the business office complies with the following requirements with respect to package delivery service workers with whom the business office has concluded an outsourcing contract:
  1. To take safety and health measures under Article 77(1) of the Occupational Safety and Health Act;
  2. To provide education on safety and health under Article 77(2) of the Occupational Safety and Health Act.
  (2) Matters relating to the supervision required under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 10 (Renewal of contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services) (1) Where a package delivery service worker requests to renew the contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services during the period between 150 days and 60 days prior to the expiration date of the contract, and the total contract terms (referring to the terms from the date of entering into the first contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services to the expiration date of such contract intended to be renewed; hereafter in this Article, the same shall apply) is six years or less, the relevant package delivery service provider (including a business office that has concluded a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services with the package delivery service provider; hereafter in this Article and Article 11, the same shall apply) shall not refuse to renew it except in any of the following cases:
  1. Cases where the package delivery service worker concluded the contract by fraud or other improper means;
  2. Cases prescribed by Presidential Decree where the package delivery service provider finds it impracticable to renew the contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services due to a serious breach, etc. by the package delivery service worker;
  3. Cases prescribed by Presidential Decree where it is impracticable for the package delivery service provider to maintain normal operations of his or her package delivery service business.
  (2) Where a package delivery service worker on the total contract terms exceeding six years requests the renewal of the contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery, the relevant package delivery service provider shall endeavor to renew the contract taking into consideration the protection of the status of the package delivery service worker and other similar matters.
  (3) A package delivery service provider that intends to refuse the request for renewal under paragraph (1) shall give written notice of the reasons for refusal to the relevant package delivery service worker, within 15 days from the date of receipt of such request.
  (4) Where a package delivery service provider fails to give notice of refusal required under paragraph (3) or fails to give written notice of change in the terms and conditions of the relevant contract or of that it is not willing to renew the relevant contract, to the relevant package delivery service worker during the period between 150 days and 60 days prior to the expiration date of the contract, the contract is deemed to be renewed under the same terms and conditions as those of the existing contract; provided, the foregoing shall not apply where the package delivery service worker raises any objection by not later than 30 days before the expiration of the contract or where a natural disaster or any other unavoidable cause prescribed by Presidential Decree occurs to the package delivery service provider or to the package delivery service worker.

Article 11 (Termination of contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services) (1) Where a package delivery service provider intends to terminate a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services concluded with a package delivery service worker, such provider shall give written notice to the package delivery service worker at least twice, specifying the details of such worker's breach of the contract and informing that the contract will be terminated if the worker fails to rectify such breach after a given grace period of at least 60 days; provided, the foregoing shall not apply where there exists any serious cause making it impracticable to continue the contract, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) Termination of a contract without fulfilling the procedures under paragraph (1) shall have no effect.
  (3) Where the registration of a package delivery service provider has been revoked under Article 15(1), the contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services between the package delivery service provider and the package delivery service worker shall be deemed terminated.

Article 12 (Permission for trucking transport services obtained by package delivery service workers) A person who intends to provide services as a package delivery service worker, by entering into a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services with a package delivery service provider or a business office, shall obtain permission for the trucking transport service under Article 3(7)1 of the Trucking Transport Business Act in compliance with the supply standards under paragraph (1) of that Article.

Article 13 (Succession to status of package delivery service providers) (1) Where a package delivery service provider transfers his or her package delivery service business or is dead or where a package delivery service provider that is a corporation is merged with another corporation, the transferee, the heir, or the surviving or newly established corporation following the merger shall succeed to the status of the previous package delivery service provider; provided, the foregoing shall not apply if the transferee of the package delivery service business or the surviving or newly established corporation following the merger falls under any of subparagraphs 1 through 4 of Article 6.
  (2) Where an heir who succeeds to the status of a package delivery service provider pursuant to paragraph (1) falls under any of subparagraphs 1 through 4 of Article 6 or where a corporation that succeeds to such status pursuant to paragraph (1) falls under subparagraph 5 of that Article, the heir shall transfer the status of the package delivery service provider to a third person, or the corporation shall replace the executive officer at issue, within six months from the date of the commencement of inheritance or the date of merger, respectively.
  (3) A person who has succeeded to the status of a package delivery service provider pursuant to paragraph (1) shall file a report with the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport on the succession within 30 days from the date a cause for the succession arises, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.
  (4) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall give notice to a person who has filed a report as to whether to accept the report within 30 days from receipt of the report under paragraph (3).
  (5) If the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport fails to give notice to a person who has filed a report as to whether to accept the report or whether to extend a processing period under a statute or regulation governing processing of civil petitions within the period prescribed in paragraph (4), the report shall be deemed to be accepted on the day following the end of that period (if such processing period is extended or re-extended under a statute or regulation governing processing of civil petitions, referring to the relevant processing period).

Article 14 (Reporting on temporary or permanent closure of package delivery service business) (1) Where a package delivery service provider intends to temporarily close all or part, or permanently close all, of his or her package delivery service business, he or she shall file a report thereon with the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport in advance, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall give notice to a person who has filed a report as to whether to accept the report within 30 days from the date of receipt of the report under paragraph (1).
  (3) If the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport fails to give notice to a person who has filed a report as to whether to accept the report or whether to extend a processing period under a statute or regulation governing processing of civil petitions within the period prescribed in paragraph (2), the report shall be deemed to be accepted on the day following the end of that period (if such processing period is extended or re-extended under a statute or regulation governing processing of civil petitions, referring to the relevant processing period).
  (4) Where a package delivery service provider intends to temporarily close all or part, or permanently close all, of his or her package delivery service business, he or she shall in advance post a notice of the intent at his or her place of business or any other place readily visible to the general public.
  (5) Where a package delivery service provider temporarily close all or part, or permanently closes all, of his or her package delivery service business, he or she shall return the motor vehicle registration certificates for, and the motor vehicle registration license plates of, trucks dedicated to package delivery services to the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 15 (Revocation of registration) (1) Where a package delivery service provider falls under any of the following cases, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may revoke the registration of the package delivery service provider; provided, in the case of subparagraph 1, 2, 4, 6, or 7, such registration shall be revoked: <Amended on Dec. 2, 2025>
  1. Where he or she has filed for registration under Article 5(1) by fraud or other improper means;
  2. Where he or she ceases to meet the requirement for registration prescribed in Article 5(1)1;
  3. Where he or she ceases to meet the requirements for registration prescribed in Article 5(1)2;
  4. Where he or she has filed for registration of change under Article 5(2) by fraud or other improper means;
  5. Where he or she has changed any registered matter without filing for registration of change under Article 5(2);
  6. Where he or she falls under any of the circumstances specified in the subparagraphs of Article 6; provided, the foregoing shall not apply in the case of subparagraph 5 of that Article where the relevant executive officer is replaced within three months from the date the relevant cause is found;
  7. Where he or she has lent the certificate of registration of package delivery service business to another person, in violation of subparagraph 1 of Article 7;
  8. Where he or she fails to use a standard contract or an entrustment contract prepared based thereon, in violation of Article 32(2);
  9. Where he or she fails to comply with an improvement order under Article 39 without good cause.
  (2) Detailed criteria for disposition made under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 16 (Prohibition of transportation for remuneration by using trucks dedicated to package delivery services for purpose other than original purpose) No person shall transport goods for remuneration by using trucks dedicated to package delivery services for a purpose other than the collection and delivery of goods eligible for package delivery services.

CHAPTER III SMALL PACKAGE DELIVERY AGENT SERVICE BUSINESS

Article 17 (Small package delivery agent service provider certification) (1) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may grant certification as a small package delivery agent service provider (hereinafter referred to as "certification") to persons who provide safe and convenient small package delivery agent services.
  (2) A person who intends to obtain the certification shall file an application with the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) A person who has obtained the certification may use a certification mark (hereinafter referred to as "certification mark") as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (4) No person who has failed to obtain the certification shall use a certification mark or any similar mark.
  (5) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may give priority to providing administrative and financial support, etc. under Article 23 to persons who have obtained the certification.
  (6) Necessary matters relating to eligibility, criteria, procedures, etc. for the certification under paragraphs (1) through (5) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 18 (Certification agent) (1) In relation to certification, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may designate a certification agent for small package delivery agent service providers (hereinafter referred to as "certification agent") to perform certification services.
  (2) A certification agent shall be designated from among the following entities as prescribed by Presidential Decree:
  1. Public institutions referred to in Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions;
  2. Government-funded research institutes defined in Article 2 of the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Research Institutes;
  3. Cooperation organizations designated for the development of industrial standardization pursuant to Article 5(3) of the Industrial Standardization Act.
  (3) The head of a certification agent may request cooperation from relevant administrative agencies and other relevant agencies if necessary for performing certification services under paragraph (1).
  (4) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may fully or partially subsidize costs incurred in performing certification services for the certification agents designated under paragraph (1) within the budget.
  (5) Where a certification agent falls under any of the following cases, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may revoke the designation; provided, in the case of subparagraph 1, such designation shall be revoked:
  1. Where it is designated by fraud or other improper means;
  2. Where it ceases to meet the requirements for designation prescribed in paragraph (6);
  3. Where it has granted certification in violation of the standards for certification under Article 17(6).
  (6) Standards and procedures for the designation of certification agents, the scope of certification services, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 19 (Revocation of certification) (1) Where a person who has obtained certification in accordance with Article 17(1) falls under any of the following cases, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may revoke the certification as prescribed by Presidential Decree; provided, in the case of subparagraph 1 or 2, such certification shall be revoked: <Amended on Jan. 16, 2024; Dec. 2, 2025>
  1. Where the person has obtained certification by fraud or other improper means;
  2. Where the person lends the certification mark to another person;
  3. Where the person ceases to meet the criteria for certification under Article 17(6);
  4. Where the person has entered into a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services, a contract for employment, etc. with a person falling under Article 19-2(1);
  5. Where the person has concluded a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services, a contract for employment, etc. with a small package delivery service worker, etc. who does not meet the driving qualifications under Article 19-4(1);
  6. Where the person has concluded a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services, a contract for employment, etc. with a small package delivery service workers, etc. who has failed to obtain insurance, etc. under Article 19-5(1);
  7. Where the person has concluded a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services, a contract for employment, etc. with a person who has not received the education under Article 19-6(1).
  (2) Where certification is revoked pursuant to paragraph (1), the person who has obtained the certification shall discontinue the use of the relevant certification mark.

Article 19-2 (Restrictions on engaging in small package delivery agency service business) (1) Any of the following persons shall be prohibited from becoming a small package delivery agent service worker:
  1. A person who has committed any of the following crimes and has been sentenced to date imprisonment without labor or heavier, and for whom the period specified by Presidential Decree has yet to elapse, considering the type and nature of crime, length of the sentence, risk of recidivism and other factors, within a maximum range of 20 years from the date their sentence was executed (including cases deemed executed) or exempted:
  a. A crime prescribed in each subparagraph of Article 2(1) of the Act on Special Cases concerning the Punishment of Specific Violent Crimes;
  b. A crime under Articles 5-2, 5-4, 5-5, 5-9, and 11 of the Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Crimes;
  c. A crime prescribed in the Narcotics Control Act;
  d. A crime under Articles 2(1)2 through 4, 3 through 9, 14, 14-2, 14-3, and 15 of the Act on Special Cases concerning the Punishment, etc. of Sexual Crimes;
  e. A crime defined in subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the Act on the Protection of Children and Youth against Sex Offenses;
  2. A person for whom the period of suspension has yet to elapse after he or she was sentenced to the suspension of execution of imprisonment without labor or heavier for a crime under subparagraph 1.
  (2) Where a certified small package delivery agent service provider or a business office (hereinafter referred to as "small package delivery agent service worker, etc.") verifies that a small package delivery agent service worker or a person who intends to become a small package delivery agent service worker (hereinafter referred to as "small package delivery agent service worker, etc.") falls under the grounds for restriction on his or her engagement as prescribed in paragraph (1), the small package delivery agent service worker or the business office shall not enter into or terminate a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services, a contract for employment, etc. with the relevant small package delivery agent service worker, etc.
  [This Article Added on Jan. 16, 2024]

Article 19-3 (Inquiry into criminal history records for verification of restrictions on working) (1) A small package delivery agent service worker or a business office shall request an inquiry of criminal history records from the commissioner of a City/Do police agency or the chief of a police station having jurisdiction over the location of a small package delivery agent service worker or a person who intends to become a small package delivery agent service worker, in accordance with Article 6 of the Act on the Lapse of Criminal Sentences, with the consent of the relevant person to verify whether he or she falls under the grounds for service restrictions under Article 19-2(1); provided, where a small package delivery agent service worker, etc. submits a written reply to criminal history records directly to the certified small package delivery agent service provider or the business office, he or she shall be deemed to have his or her criminal history records inquired.
  (2) The commissioner of a City/Do police agency or the chief of a police station in receipt of a request for inquiry into criminal records under paragraph (1) shall comply with such request without good cause.
  (3) Matters necessary for the procedures, scope, etc. of criminal history record inquiries under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Jan. 16, 2024]

Article 19-4 (Verification of driving qualification of small package delivery agent service worker, etc.) (1) A certified small package delivery agent service provider or business offices shall verify the driving qualifications (referring to a driver's license under Article 80(1) of the Road Traffic Act; hereinafter the same shall apply) of a small package delivery agent service worker, etc.
  (2) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may allow a certified small package delivery agent service provider or a business office to use the verification system of driving qualifications under Article 34-3 of the Passenger Transport Service Act in order to verify the driving qualification of a small package delivery agent service worker, etc. pursuant to paragraph (1).
  (3) If the small package delivery agent service provider, etc. does not have a driver's license upon the results of the verification under paragraph (1) (including cases where the driver's license has been suspended), the certified small package delivery agent service provider or business office shall not enter into a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services, a contract for employment, etc., with the small package delivery agent service worker, etc. or shall terminate the contract.
  (4) Matters necessary for the procedures, methods, etc. of verifying driver's qualifications under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.
  [This Article Added on Jan. 16, 2024]

Article 19-5 (Verification of insurance coverage of small package delivery agent service workers) (1) A certified small package delivery agent service provider or business office shall verify whether a small package delivery agent service provider, etc. has obtained insurance or mutual aid coverage (hereinafter referred to as “insurance, etc.”) that guarantees compensation for the death of or bodily injury to another person, or damage to another person’s property due to the operation of two-wheeled motor vehicles, etc. used in small package delivery agent services.
  (2) If the small package delivery agent service provider, etc. has not obtained insurance, etc. based on the results of the verification under paragraph (1), the certified small package delivery agent service provider or business office shall not conclude a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services, a contract for employment, etc. with the small package delivery agent service worker, etc. or shall terminate the contract.
  (3) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may establish and operate an information system (hereafter in this Article referred to as "information system") that can verify whether insurance, etc. has been obtained, and may allow certified small package delivery agent service providers or business offices to utilize the relevant information system.
  (4) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may, to establish and operate the information system, request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, the heads of local governments, the heads of public institutions under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, insurance business entities, and the heads of insurance-related organizations to provide information prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, a person requested to provide the relevant information shall comply the request unless there is a compelling reason not to do so.
  (5) A certified small package delivery agent service provider or business office may request small package delivery agency service workers, etc. to submit materials to verify whether they have obtained insurance, etc. and a person requested to submit such materials shall comply with the request unless there is a compelling reason not to do so.
  (6) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (5), matters necessary for the types of insurance, the subjects of coverage, the timing and procedures for verifying whether such coverage has been obtained, and the establishment, operation, etc. of the information system shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 2, 2025]

Article 19-6 (Education for small package delivery agency service workers) (1) A person who intends to become a small package delivery agency service worker shall, before concluding a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services, a contract for employment, etc. with a certified small package delivery agent service provider or a business office, complete traffic safety education conducted by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, a Metropolitan City Mayor, a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, a Do Governor, or a Special Self-Governing Province Governor (hereinafter referred to as the "Mayor/Do Governor"), as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.
  (2) A certified small package delivery agent service provider or a business office shall not conclude a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services, a contract for employment, etc. with a person who has not completed education under paragraph (1). 
  (3) If necessary for efficiently conducting education under paragraph (1), the Mayor/Do Governor may directly establish and operate or designate a training institute for last-mile delivery service workers, as prescribed by ordinance of the competent local government, and may provide financial support necessary for the operation of the training institute for last-mile delivery service workers.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 2, 2025]

CHAPTER IV LAYING OF FOUNDATIONS FOR LAST-MILE LOGISTICS INDUSTRY AND PROMOTION THEREOF

Article 20 (Formulation of master plans for development of last-mile logistics industry) (1) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall formulate a master plan for the development of the last-mile logistics industry (hereinafter referred to as "master plan") every five years for the development of the last-mile logistics industry.
  (2) A master plan shall include the following: <Amended on Oct. 24, 2023>
  1. Basic direction-setting for policies to develop the last-mile logistics industry;
  2. Policies for fostering each field of the last-mile logistics industry;
  3. Matters relating to the promotion of research and development of each field of the last-mile logistics industry;
  4. Matters relating to the surveys of the last-mile logistics industry, relevant statistics, establishment of information systems, etc.;
  5. Matters relating to the expansion and operation of facilities and equipment, etc. for last-mile logistics;
  6. Matters relating to the facilitation of employment and business start-up and standardization in the last-mile logistics industry;
  7. Matters relating to the improvement of the market environment for the last-mile logistics industry, including the protection of last-mile delivery service workers and consumers;
  8. Matters relating to the promotion of last-mile logistics services in logistically vulnerable areas;
  9. Other matters necessary for the development of the last-mile logistics industry.
  (3) Where the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport intends to formulate a master plan or to change any matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, he or she shall preconsult with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies thereon and shall submit the plan to the National Logistics Policies Committee established under Article 17 of the Framework Act on Logistics Policies for deliberation.

Article 21 Deleted. <Jan. 9, 2024>

Article 22 (Fact-finding surveys and compilation of statistics) (1) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may conduct a fact-finding survey on the last-mile logistics industry (hereinafter referred to as "fact-finding survey") to collect baseline data and compile statistics necessary for the development of the last-mile logistics industry.
  (2) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall compile, manage, and publish statistics on the last-mile logistics industry with reference to fact-finding survey results; and the Minister may consult with the Minister of Data and Statistics, if necessary. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) Where it is necessary for conducting fact-finding surveys, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may request the submission of necessary materials, the provision of opinions, or other similar acts, from the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, the heads of local governments, the heads of public institutions referred to in Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, last-mile logistics business operators, the heads of relevant organizations, or other similar entities. In such cases, the heads of related central administrative agencies, etc. in receipt of request for the submission of materials, the provision of opinions, or other similar acts shall cooperate on such request unless there is a compelling reason not to do so.
  (4) The cycle and subject matter of fact-finding surveys under paragraph (1); the compilation, management, and official announcement of statistics under paragraph (2); and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 23 (Administrative and financial support) The State and local governments may provide administrative and financial support for the following projects:
  1. Expansion and improvement of economic and environment-friendly facilities and equipment related to the last-mile logistics industry;
  2. Installation and improvement of facilities, such as rest facilities and last-mile logistics shelters, for the safety and health of, and working condition improvements for, last-mile delivery service workers;
  3. Creation of a model city or complex for research and technology development, and demonstration thereof for fostering the last-mile logistics industry;
  4. Consulting for increasing the efficiency of the last-mile logistics industry;
  5. Education related to the last-mile logistics industry;
  6. Other projects prescribed by Presidential Decree for the development of the last-mile logistics industry.

Article 24 (Special cases concerning taxation) The State and local governments may grant last-mile logistics service providers exemption from or reduction of tax, such as income tax, corporate tax, acquisition tax, property tax, and registration and license tax, in accordance with the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, the Restriction of Special Local Taxation Act, and other tax-related statutes, to foster the last-mile logistics industry.

Article 25 (Support for starting businesses) The State and local governments may provide administrative and financial support for the following projects to promote starting businesses related to the last-mile logistics industry:
  1. Identifying and nurturing aspiring business starters;
  2. Commercializing outstanding ideas of business starters or developing markets therefor;
  3. Supporting aspiring or actual business starters in entering overseas markets;
  4. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as support for enterprises, educational institutions, and similar entities related to business startup.

Article 26 (Development and management of professional human resources) (1) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may formulate and promote policies for the development, management, education and training, etc. of human resources with technical expertise or skills in the last-mile logistics industry (hereinafter referred to as "professional human resources").
  (2) Policies under paragraph (1) shall include the following:
  1. Matters relating to the supply of and demand for, and the use of, professional human resources;
  2. Matters relating to the development and education and training of professional human resources;
  3. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, which are necessary for the development and management of professional human resources.
  (3) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may designate a research institute, university, institution, or organization prescribed by Presidential Decree as a training institution for professional human resources and may authorize such institution to provide education and training under paragraph (1).
  (4) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may fully or partially subsidize costs incurred in providing education and training for a training institution for professional human resources designated under paragraph (3).
  (5) Where a training institution for professional human resources designated under paragraph (3) falls under any of the following cases, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may revoke the designation; provided, in the case of subparagraph 1, such designation shall be revoked:
  1. Where it has obtained the designation by fraud or other improper means;
  2. Where it fails to meet the requirements for designation as a training institution for professional human resources under paragraph (6) for at least three consecutive months.
  (6) Matters necessary for the development and management of professional human resources, the designation of training institutions for professional human resources and revocation of such designation, the subsidization for such institutions, and other relevant matters under paragraphs (1) through (5) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 27 (Promotion of standardization) (1) The Government shall establish standards for matters prescribed by Presidential Decree relating to goods packaging, storage, transportation, information systems, etc. and shall publicly notify them and may recommend last-mile logistics business operators to use the standards; provided, with regard to matters for which the Korean Industrial Standards under Article 12 of the Industrial Standardization Act have been established, such standards shall govern.
  (2) Where necessary to promote a standardization project under paragraph (1), the Government may designate a specialized institution or organization to conduct the standardization project and subsidize the institution or organization to cover all or some of the costs incurred in conducting the standardization project.

Article 28 (Implementation of pilot projects) (1) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may implement pilot projects if necessary for developing the last-mile logistics industry.
  (2) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transportation may provide financial, administrative, and technological support for persons who participate in pilot projects prescribed in paragraph (1).
  (3) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transportation shall assess the outcomes of pilot projects under paragraph (1).
  (4) Matters relating to procedures for the implementation of pilot projects under paragraph (1), means to provide support, assessment of outcomes, and other similar details shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER V SUPPORT FOR LAST-MILE LOGISTICS FACILITIES

Article 29 (Support for installation of last-mile logistics facilities) (1) The State and local governments may fully or partially subsidize or lend the costs incurred in the construction, repair, improvement, etc. of last-mile logistics facilities.
  (2) The State and local governments may give priority to providing subsidies or loans to any of the following projects: <Amended on Jun. 9, 2023>
  1. Projects for installing or improving infrastructure, such as roads, communications facilities, electric facilities, and water supply systems, necessary for the smooth development and expansion of last-mile logistics facilities;
  2. Projects implemented in growth promotion areas, areas of special concern, and rural areas as defined in Article 2 of the Special Act on Local Autonomy and Balanced Regional Development, which are aimed at addressing imbalance in last-mile logistics facilities between regions;
  3. Projects for installing or improving smart logistics centers defined in subparagraph 5-4 of Article 2 of the Act on the Development and Management of Logistics Facilities, which are necessary for the smooth development and expansion of last-mile logistics facilities;
  4. Other projects prescribed by Presidential Decree, which are necessary for the smooth provision of last-mile logistics services.
  (3) Where deemed necessary for expanding last-mile logistics facilities, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may request the head of the competent local government to cooperate in securing the building site, changing an urban or Gun plan defined in subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act (hereinafter referred to as "urban or Gun plan"), installing an urban or Gun planning facility under subparagraph 7 of that Article, or conducting any similar work.

Article 30 (Special cases concerning the Act on the Development and Management of Logistics Facilities) (1) Notwithstanding Article 50 of the Act on the Development and Management of Logistics Facilities, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may otherwise prescribe, by Presidential Decree, guidelines for prices of land in lots, facilities, etc. developed through a logistics complex development project, if necessary for supporting last-mile logistics business operators and expanding last-mile logistics facilities.
  (2) If the implementer of a logistics complex development project under Article 27 of the Act on the Development and Management of Logistics Facilities intends to dispose of land in lots, facilities, etc. developed in compliance with the guidelines for prices as prescribed under paragraph (1), the ratio of the sites for logistics facilities to be occupied and used by last-mile logistics business operators to the total area of the sites for logistics facilities in the relevant logistics complex shall exceed the standard prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 31 (Securing of last-mile logistics facilities) (1) Where any of the following projects generating new demand for last-mile logistics services with the concentration of population is implemented in an area of a local government, the head of the local government shall examine whether the appropriate securing of last-mile logistics facilities for the smooth handling of trading volume is reflected in the relevant urban or Gun plan and the master plan for regional logistics referred to in Article 14(1) of the Framework Act on Logistics Policies:
  1. Public housing projects defined in subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Special Act on Public Housing;
  2. Enterprise city development projects defined in subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Special Act on the Development of Enterprise Cities;
  3. Urban development projects under Article 2(1)2 of the Urban Development Act;
  4. Regional development projects defined in subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Regional Development Assistance Act;
  5. Housing site development projects defined in subparagraph 4 of Article 2 of the Housing Site Development Promotion Act;
  6. Other projects prescribed by Presidential Decree that generate demand for last-mile logistics services.
  (2) Where the head of a local government deems that last-mile logistics facilities are insufficient after the examination under paragraph (1), he or she shall reflect the securing of last-mile logistics facilities to reach an appropriate scale in the relevant urban or Gun plan and the master plan for regional logistics under Article 14(1) of the Framework Act on Logistics Policies, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER VI PROTECTION OF LAST-MILE DELIVERY SERVICE WORKERS AND IMPROVEMENT OF QUALITY OF THEIR SERVICES

Article 32 (Standard contract) (1) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall prepare and distribute a standard contract for last-mile logistics services, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, for the conclusion of a fair contract among a last-mile logistics business operator, a business office, and a last-mile delivery service worker and may recommend such business operator, business office, and service worker to use it. <Amended on Dec. 2, 2025>
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), when a package delivery service provider, a business office, and a package delivery service worker concludes a contract for entrustment of transportation with one another under Article 8, they shall either use the standard contract under paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as the “standard contract”) or an entrustment contract prepared by the package delivery service provider based on the standard contract (hereinafter referred to as the “entrustment contract”). In such cases, the contents that shall be included in the entrustment contract, such as the service area entrusted to the business office or package delivery service workers, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added on Dec. 2, 2025>
  (3) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may give priority to providing administrative and financial support, etc. under Article 23 for last-mile logistics business operators who use the standard contract. <Amended on Dec. 2, 2025>
  [Title Amended on Dec. 2, 2025]

Article 33 (Service terms and conditions) (1) Last-mile logistics business operators shall prepare terms and conditions for last-mile logistics services (hereinafter referred to as "service terms and conditions") and file a report thereon with the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport. The foregoing shall also apply where any change of such terms and conditions is intended.
  (2) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall give notice to a person who has filed a report as to whether to accept the report within 30 days from the date of receipt of the report or of the report of change under paragraph (1).
  (3) If the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport fails to give notice to a person who has filed a report as to whether to accept the report or whether to extend a processing period under a statute or regulation governing processing of civil petitions within the period prescribed in paragraph (2), the report shall be deemed to be accepted on the day following the end of that period (if such processing period is extended or re-extended under a statute or regulation governing processing of civil petitions, referring to the relevant processing period).
  (4) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may recommend last-mile logistics business operators to use the standard terms and conditions for last-mile logistics services (hereinafter referred to as "standard terms and conditions"), if any, examined by the Fair Trade Commission pursuant to Article 19-3 of the Act on the Regulation of Terms and Conditions.
  (5) If a last-mile logistics business operator consents to the use of the standard terms and conditions when he or she files for registration pursuant to Article 5(1) (including filing for registration of change thereof under Article 5(2)) or obtains certification pursuant to Article 17(1), such operator shall be deemed to have filed a report pursuant to paragraph (1).
  (6) Where a last-mile logistics business operator has filed a report on the service terms and conditions or on any change of them pursuant to paragraph (1), he or she shall disclose the service terms and conditions on the operator's website and keep them at a place readily visible to consumers to make them available to the consumers for perusal.
  (7) Details to be included in the service terms and conditions referred to in paragraph (1), procedures for reporting, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 34 (Prohibition of receiving or providing unlawful profits) (1) No person, other than a last-mile logistics business operator, a business office, or a last-mile delivery service worker, shall unlawfully receive all or part of an amount of money paid by a consumer in exchange for last-mile logistics services.
  (2) No last-mile logistics business operator, business office, or last-mile delivery service worker shall unlawfully rebate an amount equivalent to all or part of an amount of money received in exchange for providing services to a person who has requested the delivery of goods, or a last-mile business operator or a business office that is the counterparty to a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services, a contract for employment, etc.
  (3) Types of and criteria for the acts of receiving unlawful profits or making unlawful rebates under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 35 (Assessment of last-mile logistics services) (1) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may assess last-mile logistics services provided by last-mile logistics business operators (hereinafter referred to as "assessment of services") to improve the quality of last-mile logistics services, to protect the rights and interests of last-mile delivery service workers and consumers, and to conduct any other similar activities.
  (2) Criteria for the assessment of services shall be as follows: <Amended on Oct. 24, 2023; Jan. 16, 2024; Dec. 2, 2025>
  1. Consumer satisfaction with last-mile logistics services;
  2. Stability of last-mile logistics services;
  3. Promotion of the rights and interests of last-mile delivery service workers and consumers;
  4. Improvement of the quality of last-mile logistics services, including the level of service charges in logistically vulnerable areas;
  5. Appropriateness of working hours and safety of working environment for last-mile delivery service workers;
  6.Other matters equivalent to subparagraph 1 through 5 as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.
  (3) Service evaluation shall include a survey of consumers and last-mile delivery service workers, and matters necessary for detailed evaluation methods and procedures, etc. shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport. <Amended on Jan. 16, 2024>
  (4) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may officially announce details, such as the results of assessment by item, after conducting the assessment of services under paragraph (1), as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (5) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may grant awards to persons showing outstanding results in assessments as prescribed by Presidential Decree and may give priority to providing administrative or financial support for such persons under Article 23.
  (6) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may request the provision of information prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the purchase of industrial accident compensation insurance under Article 125 of the Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Act, from the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service established under Article 10 of that Act, in order to assess matters relating to the promotion of rights and interests of last-mile delivery service workers prescribed in paragraph (2)3. In such cases, the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service shall comply with such request unless there is a compelling reason not to do so.
  (7) For assessing services, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may request a last-mile logistics business operator to submit relevant materials, to give opinions, and to perform other similar activities or may conduct an on-site investigation on relevant services, as prescribed by Presidential Decree; and the last-mile logistics business operator so requested shall comply with such request unless there is a compelling reason not to do so.

Article 36 (Protection of last-mile delivery service workers) (1) A last-mile logistics business operator shall endeavor to ensure the safety of last-mile delivery service workers with respect to the following: <Amended on Dec. 2, 2025>
  1. Provision of break time and a place to rest necessary to prevent overwork by last-mile delivery service workers and to ensure their safety;
  2. Securing of sufficient spaces and facilities, such as runways and last mile delivery ramps at loading docks, necessary for the safe operation of vehicles in last-mile logistics facilities;
  3. Preparation of safety measures in case last-mile delivery service workers have difficulty in conducting business activities due to harsh weather, such as extreme heat or cold or heavy rain or snow;
  4. Prevention of inducing last-mile delivery service workers to engage in excessive driving that may cause overwork or accidents.
  (2) A last-mile logistics business operator shall be equipped with a rest facility that last-mile delivery service workers can use during their break time as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 37 (Last-mile logistics shelters) (1) The State and local governments may establish and operate last-mile logistics shelters to promote the rights and interests of last-mile delivery service workers.
  (2) The functions of last-mile logistics shelters shall be as follows:
  1. Provision of rest and welfare space for last-mile delivery service workers;
  2. Provision of facilities for maintenance of last-mile delivery service workers' vehicles of transportation;
  3. Support for the job-seeking of last-mile delivery service workers, such as counseling on work and employment;
  4. Other matters prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, for the protection of last-mile delivery service workers and improvement of their welfare.
  (3) Other matters necessary for the establishment and management of last-mile logistics shelters shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 38 (Obligation to improve services) (1) Last-mile logistics business operators, business offices, and last-mile delivery service workers shall endeavor to secure the safe delivery of goods to consumers that is outsourced to them, in accordance with the principle of good faith. <Amended on Jan. 16, 2024>
  (2) A certified small package delivery agent service provider or a business office shall endeavor to educate small package delivery agency service workers, etc. on the compliance with traffic rules. <Added on Jan. 16, 2024>

Article 39 (Improvement order and recommendation) Where the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport deems it necessary to ensure the quality and safety of last-mile logistics services, enhance consumer convenience, ensure the safety of last-mile delivery service workers, or protect their rights and interests, he or she may order a package delivery service provider to take any of the following measures or recommend that a certified small package delivery agent service provider take any of the following measures: <Amended on Jan. 9, 2024; Dec. 2, 2025>
  1. Measures for the safe delivery of goods;
  2. Improvement of last-mile logistics facilities and equipment;
  3. Management of business offices to which business affairs are outsourced under Article 8;
  3-2. Establishment of safety measures to create a safe working environment for last-mile logistics services workers;
  3-3. Development of measures to protect the rights and interests of last-mile delivery service workers and improve their treatment; 
  3-4. Measures regarding the results of the joint safety inspection under Article 44-2; 
  4. To change service terms and conditions;
  5. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, which are necessary to improve last-mile logistics services.

CHAPTER VII LAST-MILE LOGISTICS TRADE ASSOCIATION

Article 40 (Establishment of association) (1) Certified small package delivery agent service providers may establish an association related to small package delivery agent services (hereinafter referred to as the "Association") if necessary for the sound development of the last-mile logistics industry and the promotion of common interests.
  (2) The Association shall be a corporation.
  (3) In order for the Association to be established, authorization from the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall be obtained as prescribed by Presidential Decree. The same shall apply where the Association intends to amend its articles of incorporation.
  (4) The Association shall be formed upon filing for registration of its establishment after obtaining authorization for the establishment thereof referred to in paragraph (3).
  (5) Except as provided in this Act, the provisions of the Civil Act governing incorporated associations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Association.
  (6) Where it is necessary for the development of the Association, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may provide administrative and financial support for the Association.
  (7) Matters necessary for the establishment of the Association, authorization for its establishment, operations of projects, and other similar details shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 41 (Establishment of mutual aid association) (1) Certified small package delivery agent service providers may establish a mutual aid association (hereinafter referred to as the "Mutual Aid Association") with authorization from the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, in order to support its members' independent economic activities and to compensate damage caused by accidents occurring in the use of vehicles for business purposes by its members, through mutual cooperative organizations.
  (2) The Mutual Aid Association shall be a corporation and shall be formed upon filling for registration of its establishment at the location of its principal office.
  (3) Members of the Mutual Aid Association shall pay contributions necessary for mutual aid programs.
  (4) Matters relating to qualifications for membership of the Mutual Aid Association and its executive officers and other matters necessary for its operation shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
  (5) Matters to be entered in the articles of incorporation of the Mutual Aid Association, the operation and supervision thereof, and other relevant matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 42 (Programs of mutual aid association) (1) The Mutual Aid Association shall conduct the following programs:
  1. Mutual aid services to cover the liability of a member for damage caused by an accident occurring in the use of his or her vehicle for business purposes and for damage to the loads;
  2. Mutual aid services to cover damage caused to a member's vehicle for business purposes by an accident occurring while he or she possesses, uses, or manages the vehicle;
  3. Mutual aid services to cover a small package delivery agent service worker's bodily injury caused by an accident occurring while he or she possesses, uses, or manages its relevant member's vehicle for business purposes;
  4. Mutual aid services to cover losses sustained by employees of the Mutual Aid Association due to accidents on duty;
  5. Establishment, operation, and management of common use facilities and other programs for the promotion of its members' convenience and welfare;
  6. Surveys and research projects to improve the management of small package delivery agent service business;
  7. Other programs incidental to those specified in subparagraphs 1 through 6, which are prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
  (2) When the Mutual Aid Association intends to conduct a mutual aid program specified in paragraph (1)1 through 4, it shall establish regulations on mutual aid and obtain authorization from the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport. The same shall also apply to amendments to the regulations on mutual aid.
  (3) The regulations on mutual aid referred to in paragraph (2) shall include guidelines necessary to operate mutual aid programs such as the scope of the mutual aid programs, the details of mutual aid contracts and contributions, mutual aid benefits, liability reserve funds to cover mutual aid benefits, and the appropriation and accumulation of reserves.
  (4) The Insurance Business Act shall not apply to mutual aid programs referred to in paragraph (1)1 through 4.
  (5) Either party to a dispute over a mutual aid agreement or the payment of mutual aid benefits or to any other dispute arising in connection with a mutual aid program conducted under paragraph (1) may apply for mediation to the Committee for Guaranteeing Motor Vehicle Accident Compensation under Article 23-3 of the Compulsory Motor Vehicle Liability Security Act. <Amended on Jan. 9, 2024>

CHAPTER VIII SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 43 (Guidance and supervision) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall guide and supervise the affairs under the authority of the heads of local governments as prescribed in this Act, to promote the rational development of the last-mile logistics industry.

Article 44 (Reporting and inspections) (1) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may, in any of the following cases, require a last-mile logistics business operator or a business office to give a report or submit a document regarding business operations or the ownership or use of vehicles of transportation; and if necessary, the Minister may require public officials under his or her jurisdiction to enter the place of business of such operator or office to inspect books, documents, or other objects or to inquire of relevant persons: <Amended on Dec. 2, 2025>
  1. Where it is necessary to check whether such operator or such office meets the requirements for registration under Article 5(1) or complies with the standards for certification under Article 17(6);
  2. Where it is necessary to ascertain the acts of disturbing the order of the market for last-mile logistics services, such as receipt or provision of unlawful profits under Article 34 or other similar acts;
  3. Where it is necessary to check whether a last-mile logistics business operator, a business office, or a last-mile delivery service worker has violated this Act;
  4. Where it is necessary to render an administrative disposition, such as revocation of registration of package delivery service business or revocation of certification of a certified small package delivery agent service provider;
  5. Where a death occurs at the business place of a last-mile logistics business operator or a business office, and it is necessary to determine the cause of death. 
  (2) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may, in any of the following cases, require the last-mile logistics business operator to report on such facility, etc. or may have public officials under his or her jurisdiction enter the relevant place of business to inspect books, documents, and other articles, or inquire of relevant persons: <Added on Jan. 9, 2024; Dec. 2, 2025> 
  1. Where necessary to verify compliance with the matters under each subparagraph of Article 36(1);
  2. Where necessary to verify whether a rest facility has been provided in accordance with Article 36(2). 
  (3) A public official who enters the place of business or conducts an inspection under paragraph (1) or (2) shall carry identification indicating his or her authority and present it to the relevant persons. <Amended on Jan. 9, 2024>

Article 44-2 (Joint safety inspection) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may, jointly with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, conduct safety inspections of the business place of a last-mile logistics business operator or a business office to ensure the safety of last-mile delivery service workers.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 2, 2025]

Article 45 (Hearings) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall hold a hearing to make any of the following dispositions:
  1. Revocation of registration under Article 15(1);
  2. Revocation of designation under Article 18(5);
  3. Revocation of certification under Article 19(1);
  4. Revocation of designation as a training institution for professional human resources under Article 26(5).

Article 46 (Delegation of authority and entrustment of affairs) (1) Part of the authority of the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport under this Act may be delegated to the head of an agency under his or her jurisdiction or the "Mayor/Do Governor", as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Dec. 2, 2025>
  (2) The Mayor/Do Governor may re-delegate part of the authority that the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport delegates to him or her under paragraph (1), to the head of a Si/Gun/Gu (the head of a Gu refers to the head of an autonomous Gu), with approval from the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.
  (3) Part of the affairs of the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport or the heads of other administrative agencies under this Act may be entrusted to relevant institutions, organizations, or corporations, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 47 (Fees) (1) A person who intends to file for registration, certification, etc. or to file a report under this Act shall pay fees prescribed by Presidential Decree; provided, where the relevant services are performed on behalf of the Minister under Article 18(1) or the relevant affairs are entrusted under Article 46(3), such person shall pay fees determined by the relevant entity performing such services or duties, to the entity.
  (2) Fees under the proviso of paragraph (1) shall be determined autonomously by relevant entities for each type of affairs in accordance with the guidelines prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 48 (Legal fiction as public officials for purposes of applying penalty provisions) Persons who perform the services as agents under Article 18(1) or who conduct the affairs entrusted under Article 46(3) shall be deemed public officials for purposes of applying Article 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act.

CHAPTER IX PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 49 (Penalty provisions) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than two years or by a fine not exceeding 20 million won:
  1. A person who conducts his or her package delivery service business by using trucks dedicated to package delivery services, without filing for registration under Article 5(1);
  2. A person who has filed for registration under Article 5(1) by fraud or other improper means and conducts his or her package delivery service business;
  3. A person who allows another person to conduct package delivery service business under his or her name or trade name, who lends his or her certificate of registration to another person, who conducts package delivery service business under another person's name or trade name, or who borrows another person's certificate of registration or assists to do so, in violation of Article 7;
  4. A person who has transported goods for remuneration by using trucks dedicated to package delivery services, for a purpose other than the collection and delivery of goods eligible for package delivery services, in violation of Article 16.

Article 50 (Joint penalty provisions) If the representative of a corporation, or an agent or employee of, or any other person employed by, a corporation or an individual commits a violation described in Article 49 in conducting the business affairs of the corporation or individual, the corporation or individual shall be punished by a fine prescribed in that Article, in addition to punishing the violator accordingly; provided, the foregoing shall not apply where the corporation or individual has not been negligent in giving due attention to and supervision over the relevant business affairs to prevent the violation.

Article 51 (Administrative fines) (1) Any of the following persons shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 5 million won: <Amended on Jan. 16, 2024; Dec. 2, 2025>
  1. A person who fails to file for registration of change under Article 5(2) or who has filed for registration of change under Article 5(2) by fraud or other improper means;
  2. A person who fails to file a report on requirements for registration under Article 5(4);
  3. A person who, in violation of Article 10(1), refuses to renew a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services without good cause;
  4. A person who fails to file a report on succession to status under Article 13(3) after an inheritance, transfer, acquisition by transfer, or merger;
  5. A person who fails to file a report on temporary or permanent closure of business under Article 14(1);
  6. A person who, in violation of Article 14(5), fails to return the motor vehicle registration certificates for, and motor vehicle license plates of, trucks dedicated to package delivery services;
  7. A person who has obtained certification under Article 17(1) by fraud or other improper means;
  8. A person who, in violation of Article 17(4), uses a certification mark or any similar mark;
  9. A person who, in violation of Article 19(2), fails to discontinue the use of a certification mark;
  9-2. A certified small package delivery agent service provider or a business office that, in violation of Article 19-2(2), fails to terminate the contract without good causes within 1 month from the date on which it is confirmed that the contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services, a contract for employment, etc. shall be terminated;
  9-3. A certified small package delivery agent service provider or a business office that, in violation of Article 19-3(1), fails to verify the criminal record of a small package delivery agent service worker, etc.;
  9-4. A certified small package delivery agent service provider or a business office that, in violation of Article 19-4(1) or (3), fails to verify the driving qualifications of small package delivery agent service workers, etc. or fails to terminate a contract, such as a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services or a contract for employment, within 1 month from the date it was determined that termination was required, without good cause; 
  9-5. A certified small package delivery agent service provider or a business office that, in violation of Article 19-5(1) or (2), fails to verify whether a small package delivery agent service worker, etc. has obtained insurance, etc., or fails to terminate a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services or a contract for employment, etc., within 1 month from the date it was determined that such termination was required, without good cause; 
  9-6. A certified small package delivery agent service provider or a business office that, in violation of Article 19-6(2), has concluded a contract for outsourcing package transport and delivery services or a contract for employment, etc. with a person who has failed to complete traffic safety education; 
  10. A package delivery service provider or a business office that, in violation of Article 32(2), has failed to use a standard contract or an entrustment contract;
  11. A person who fails to file a report on service terms and conditions or a report on changes in them under Article 33(1);
  12. A person who has received unlawful profits, in violation of Article 34, or who has made unlawful rebates (excluding where that act is, for the same reason, subject to a corrective measure under Article 24 of the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act, a penalty surcharge under Article 24-2(1) of that Act, or a penalty under subparagraph 2 of Article 67 of that Act);
  13. A person who refuses to submit materials, etc. or to undergo an on-site investigation requested for the assessment of services under Article 35(7) without good cause or who submits false materials, etc.;
  14. Where a package delivery service provider fails to comply with an improvement order issued under Article 39 without good cause;
  15. A person who fails to give a report under Article 44 without good cause or gives a false report; who fails to submit a document or submits false document; or who refuses, obstructs, or evades an inspection.
  (2) Administrative fines under paragraph (1) shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
